title: Grateful Dead Live at Memorial Coliseum on 1973-06-24
lineage: Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.02 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Good soundboard recording that improves after a rough start, highlighted by a stellar Dark Star > Eyes > China Doll medley and strong second‑set energy.
ai_review.review: The Miller soundboard capture has a messy first few tracks – a cut in I Know You Rider, reversed channels and a thin mix on Billy’s kit – but settles into solid, clear audio for the bulk of the show. Musically the concert is uneven: the first set wanders with lyrical flubs and a weak Row Jimmy, while the second set shines, especially the Dark Star‑Eyes‑China Doll sequence and standout moments from Bertha, China Cat Sunflower and Stella Blue.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance 4–5 stars and praise the Dark Star medley; recording issues are noted but limited to early tracks, yielding an overall strong show with good‑to‑very‑good audio.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early tracks are muddy and have a cut in I Know You Rider; channels reversed and slight pitch fastness noted; Billy Cobham’s kit sounds under‑mixed at the start. After ~½ hour the mix becomes clear and balanced.

standout_songs: Dark Star > Eyes of the World > China Doll
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is uneven with scattered peaks; second set is cohesive and builds to a powerful Dark Star medley. Overall pacing improves after the midway point.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His playing on Dark Star is described as "special" and generally strong throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work receives high praise, especially during the Dark Star jam; noted for a jazzy vamp that pulls listeners in.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards are called “amazing” on several tracks (e.g., Mexicali Blues, China Cat Sunflower).
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy’s kit sounds poorly mixed at the beginning of the show.
